text:
Minnesota arrives on a three-game win streak, most recently 3-1 at Utah, though the Wild are missing Marcus Foligno and Nick Foligno. The Islanders won in a shootout at Nashville, where Brayden Schenn reached 300 career goals. They're also short-handed, without Matias Maccelli and Calum Ritchie, both on injured reserve. With them out, Bo Horvat has moved beside Cizikas and Holmstrom, and Simon Holmstrom is up to 21:15 a night from 15:43. Kirill Kaprizov sits two points from 500 for his career.

Our numbers favor Minnesota, 3.44 expected goals to 2.65. At five on five, the Wild have taken 56% of the expected goals (a measure of chance quality) in their games to the Islanders' 49%. The special-teams matchup to watch is Minnesota's power play, which creates 0.95 expected goals a game, against a New York penalty kill allowing 0.88. The Islanders take 4.5 penalties a game. In net, projected starters Jesper Wallstedt (+9.9 goals saved above expected this season, meaning saves beyond what the shots should have produced) and Ilya Sorokin (+6.6) both look sharp. Sorokin was at +22.3 last season; Wallstedt was at +5.8.

Kaprizov is our top scorer pick at 51%, with goals in three straight games. Horvat is New York's best at 37%, and Matthew Schaefer has a five-game point streak. Our under-the-radar pick is Yakov Trenin, a third-liner at 12% to score whose shots have been dangerous lately: 2.0 expected goals in his last 10 games.
